# 1 Enoch Chapter 99 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Epistle of Enoch — Woe Oracles

---

**1** Woe to you who live as though God doesn't exist, who celebrate and applaud deception — you will perish and your life will come to nothing good.

**2** Woe to those who twist the meaning of what is right, who break the eternal law and remake themselves into something they were never meant to be — they will be crushed underfoot on the earth.

**3** And you, the righteous — in those days, prepare yourselves. Lift your prayers up as a living record. Set them before the angels as testimony, so that the angels can bring the sins of sinners as evidence before the Most High.

**4** In those days the nations will be thrown into turmoil, and every family of every nation will rise up on the day of their destruction.

**5** In those days desperate people will go out, grab their children, and then abandon them — leaving them to die. They will abandon infants still at the breast and never come back to them. All love for their own children will be gone.

**6** And I swear to you again, sinners: sin is stockpiled, ready for a day of endless bloodshed.

**7** Those who bow down to stones, to gold and silver images, to wooden and clay idols, to impure spirits and demons — worshipping ignorantly, without any true knowledge — not one of these things will help them. Not one.

**8** Idolatry will turn them into godless people. Their hearts will fill with terror. Their eyes will go blind from fear and nightmare visions.

**9** This is what idolatry does: it fills you with fear and godlessness. They built their whole lives on a lie; they worshipped stone. So they will perish in an instant.

**10** But in those days — blessed are all who receive the words of wisdom and take them to heart, who keep to the paths of the Most High and walk in his righteousness, and who refuse to join the godless in their godlessness. They will be saved.

**11** Woe to you who infect your neighbors with evil — you will be killed in Sheol.

**12** Woe to you who use false scales and rigged measures, who spread bitterness across the earth — you will be completely consumed by it.

**13** Woe to those who build their houses on other people's labor — where every brick and stone is made of exploitation. I am telling you: you will have no peace.

**14** Woe to those who throw away the law and the eternal inheritance of their ancestors to chase after idols — they will never rest.

**15** Woe to those who do wrong, who enable oppression, who kill their neighbors — right up until the day of the great judgment.

**16** When that day comes: God will smash your glory and fill your hearts with suffering. He will unleash his fierce wrath and cut you all down with the sword. And every holy and righteous person will remember what you did.

---

*PNEUMA notes: V. 5 is one of the darkest verses in the entire Epistle — social collapse so total that nursing mothers abandon their infants. The contrast with v. 10's beatitude is stunning. V. 13 is the woe that most directly echoes the prophets: "built their houses not with their own labor" = Jeremiah 22:13. The Epistle's woe cycle reaches its comprehensive peak here, covering idolatry, false weights, exploitative construction, ancestral law, and murder.*
